newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Goodman would consider share buy-back.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Goodman would consider share buy-back.

text.p: Australasian food group Goodman Fielder said that the sale of its European milling and bakery group had given it the opportunity to develop its local operations, with a share buy-back one possible use of the funds.
Goodman's on Friday announced the sale of its Eurpoean buisness arm, Meneba NV, for slightly more than A$300 million.
Goodman chief executive Daid Hearn said in a television interview screened on Sunday that the European sale was a "stand-alone decision because we think we're not the best owner of that business".
The funds freed up and the time that would now not have to be devoted to Meneba would now be used in developing the Australasian business.

"Clearly by exiting our European business, and we have a lot of flexibility now, the balance sheet is very strong and we've got plenty of options to take up with if the right opportunity arises," Hearn said.

Goodman's were looking at a number of opportunities, but did not presently have a limit on either length or price, he said. Whether any acquisitions would be a number of smaller purchases or one larger one was also not decided.
However, Goodman's saw a purchase of global food manufacturer Burns, Philp & Co as being too big, Hearn said.
Hearn also said that the proceeds of the Meneba sale should not make the company a takeover target, and said that a share buy-back would be considered.
"I'm not averse to in some form of returning the capital to shareholders," he said, but added he did not want to give it back only to seek to raise capital a short time later.
"So I have no 'in principle' problem with returning the money to the shareholders and we may well consider doing that some time in the future," Hearn said.
